findings.text: non-blocking: for a queue-lifted hold the row keeps the classifier's next_action, which reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1830 fixes to 'reckon crew queue release --run <id>' for every unlaunched HELD_PHASE request, and keeps recovery='resume' from RECOVERY_VERBS['held'], so a row drawn waiting still hands the coordinator the release command the change's own comment says nothing a coordinator does lifts; acting on it launches over the admission pass's automatic release path.

non-blocking: the non-review branch of _coordinator_hold_next_action re-composes 'reckon crew queue release --run <id>', a command the repository already composes for the same held population at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1830 and again at reckon/crew/obligations.py:3948; the addition duplicates that composition instead of extending an owner, so the copies can drift apart.

non-blocking: _bucket_of still takes a classification argument it now ignores, and a search over the reviewed head finds no production caller at all, only tests, so the edit to it changes no runtime surface; the live counter is _fleet_counts (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2068) plus NEEDS_ACTION (reckon/crew/ticker.py:270).

non-blocking: the launched-run case asserts count agreement only through _bucket_of, which no production code calls, so a regression in _fleet_counts for the launched held population would leave this case green; the queue-parked and coordinator-hold cases assert _fleet_counts directly and are guarded.

non-blocking: the artifacts line reports '1 EXIT=124' over the 57 importer files, but logs/per-file-head3 ends EXIT=124 in test_a_promotions_review_lookups_cost_the_same_at_any_store_size.py.log, test_a_runs_view_checks_only_the_rows_it_returns.py.log and test_crew.py.log (44 EXIT=0, 10 EXIT=1, 3 EXIT=124), so the done_when's importer population is established over 54 of 57 files and the record understates what went unmeasured.
